name: Mandalorian Clans
source_refs: Edge of the Empire Core Rulebook
overview: The Mandalorian Clans are a warrior culture organized into clan-based Houses, united by shared traditions of combat, honor, and beskar armor rather than by species or homeworld. Devastated by centuries of conflict and Imperial occupation, Mandalore's population has fallen to roughly four million, surviving in bio-dome cities on a scarred homeworld. The clans are deeply fractured between the pacifist New Mandalorians, the militant Death Watch remnants, and the pragmatic Protectors — all competing for the right to define what it means to be Mandalorian.
short_descriptor: Honor-based, clan-specific, and longer in memory than you'd expect. A debt to one Mandalorian is not a debt to all of them. A slight to one may as well be.

witness_statement.text: Fought alongside a Mandalorian squad on Carlac. Hired guns, same as me. The difference was in the quiet moments — they didn't brag, didn't posture. They maintained their gear like it was a religious act. When the shooting started, they moved like one animal with eight arms. I've worked with spec-ops teams that weren't half as tight. After the job, the clan leader thanked me by name and said I had a standing invitation. I don't think she says that to many people.
witness_statement.source: Freelance mercenary, post-engagement debrief, Outer Rim waystation

how_they_operate.heading: CLANS AND HOUSES
how_they_operate.text: Mandalorian society is organized into clans grouped under larger Houses, with authority flowing from clan chieftains up to House leaders and, when one is recognized, a single Mand'alor who speaks for all Mandalorians. Warriors swear loyalty to their clan first; inter-clan cooperation requires negotiation between chieftains or a recognized Mand'alor's direct command.

how_they_operate.heading: THE RESOL'NARE
how_they_operate.text: The Resol'nare — the Six Actions — defines Mandalorian identity: wearing armor, speaking Mando'a, defending oneself and family, raising children as Mandalorians, contributing to the clan's welfare, and rallying to the Mand'alor's call.

how_they_operate.heading: WARRIOR CULTURE
how_they_operate.text: Every adult trains for combat from childhood, making the entire population a potential militia, though standing military forces are organized into professional units like the Protectors of Concord Dawn.

how_they_operate.heading: THE HOMEWORLD
how_they_operate.text: The current population of roughly four million survives in bio-dome cities on a homeworld scarred by centuries of warfare, under Imperial occupation administered by Viceroy Gar Saxon.

how_they_operate.heading: A FRACTURED PEOPLE
how_they_operate.text: The clans remain deeply fractured — New Mandalorian pacifists, Death Watch militants, and Protector pragmatists each claim to represent the true path forward, with the Darksaber serving as the contested symbol of legitimate authority.

secondary: Reclaim Mandalorian independence from Imperial occupation
Resolve the ideological schism between pacifist and warrior factions
Preserve beskar smithing traditions and armor heritage
Restore Mandalore's standing as a sovereign power
motivations.notes: Mandalorian motivations are fractured along factional lines. The New Mandalorians sought peace and diplomatic legitimacy. Death Watch pursued militant restoration of warrior traditions. The Protectors attempted pragmatic survival under Imperial rule. What unites them is the conviction that Mandalorian identity — however defined — must endure. The Darksaber serves as the symbolic focal point for legitimacy.

strategic: Survive as a distinct culture under Imperial occupation without being absorbed or destroyed
Reunify the clans under a single Mand'alor who can command broad legitimacy
Reclaim sovereignty over Mandalore and end the Imperial Viceroy system
Preserve the beskar forging traditions and warrior heritage for future generations
operational: Maintain clan cohesion and supply lines despite Imperial resource restrictions
Navigate the Imperial Viceroy's demands without provoking full military crackdown
Identify and neutralize internal threats from Death Watch extremists and Imperial collaborators
Secure beskar ore and smithing materials through legitimate trade or covert acquisition

avoided: Assassination of fellow Mandalorians — internal disputes are settled by combat or council, not poison
Deception that compromises clan honor — lies between clans damage the fabric that holds the culture together
Surrender of beskar armor — armor is identity, and relinquishing it is unthinkable for traditionalists
methods.notes: Mandalorian methods vary sharply by faction. The Protectors favor disciplined military action and pragmatic negotiation. Death Watch remnants use infiltration, coercion, and targeted violence. New Mandalorian holdouts rely on diplomacy and institutional leverage. All factions, however, share a preference for direct action over subterfuge — Mandalorians as a culture value confrontation over deception.

strengths: Individual Mandalorian warriors are among the galaxy's most formidable combatants — beskar armor, crushgaunts, and jetpacks give tactical superiority
Clan loyalty creates tight-knit units with exceptional unit cohesion and willingness to sacrifice for each other
Fang fighters and Mandalorian starfighter tactics are respected even by Imperial Navy strategists
Cultural emphasis on martial training means every adult Mandalorian is combat-capable, not just dedicated soldiers
The Darksaber and Mand'alor tradition provide a mechanism for rapid unification when a legitimate leader emerges
weaknesses: Ideological fractures between New Mandalorian, Death Watch, and Protector factions prevent unified military or political action across the clans.
Total Mandalorian population has been reduced to approximately four million, insufficient to sustain prolonged attrition warfare against any major galactic power.
Imperial occupation under Viceroy Gar Saxon restricts clan access to military assets, beskar ore, and freedom of movement between systems.
Inter-clan rivalries and honor-based disputes divert leadership attention and warrior resources away from external threats.
Concentration of the surviving population in bio-dome cities on a scarred homeworld creates high-value, geographically fixed targets vulnerable to orbital bombardment or siege.

behavior_under_threat.low: Clans assess the threat through scouts and intelligence. Internal debate over response. No unified action unless a single clan is directly targeted.
behavior_under_threat.medium: The threatened clan mobilizes its warriors. Allied clans offer support based on existing obligations. The Protectors attempt to mediate if the threat is Imperial to avoid escalation.
behavior_under_threat.high: Multiple clans coordinate a military response. Beskar-armored warriors deploy with Fang fighter support. Death Watch elements may act unilaterally, complicating coordinated strategy.
behavior_under_threat.critical: A call for unification under the Mand'alor — if one exists. All clans set aside internal disputes to face the existential threat. Historical precedent shows Mandalorians at their most dangerous when cornered.

chain_of_command: Clan warriors on patrol or garrison
alert_escalation.notes: Mandalorian communication within a clan is fast and direct — warriors report to their chieftain without bureaucratic delay. Escalation between clans is slower and politically fraught, requiring negotiation between House leaders. The absence of a universally recognized Mand'alor means there is no single authority to coordinate a multi-clan response, creating dangerous delays when speed matters most.

tension_patterns: Clans are split between Imperial cooperation and covert resistance as competing definitions of honorable conduct, with both positions carrying legitimate precedent in Mandalorian tradition.
Darksaber-based authority claims are contested when the methods of acquisition — inheritance, combat, or seizure — do not satisfy all clan traditions simultaneously.
Imperial Viceroy demands for warrior conscription or beskar confiscation periodically push Protector-aligned clans past the threshold of pragmatic compliance.
Former Death Watch operatives embedded in post-war governance structures use coercion and political leverage to advance militant agendas from within institutional positions.
Resource scarcity under Imperial occupation forces clans into dealings with criminal syndicates, undermining the moral authority that clan leadership depends on for internal cohesion.

mcguffin_interest.notes: Mandalorians are most interested in weapons (especially beskar-related arms and armor) and artifacts (the Darksaber, clan relics, historical items that confer legitimacy). Data matters when it reveals Imperial plans for Mandalore or the location of lost clan holdings. Persons of interest include missing clan members, potential Mand'alor candidates, and Imperial officials who can be leveraged. Contraband holds little cultural value.

relationship_notes.imperial_military: The Empire occupies Mandalore through Viceroy Gar Saxon. The Protectors cooperate pragmatically while most clans view the occupation as an intolerable humiliation. Open rebellion has been suppressed but never truly extinguished.
relationship_notes.rebel_alliance: Some Mandalorian clans — particularly those aligned with Clan Wren — have cooperated with the Rebellion. The relationship is tactical rather than ideological; Mandalorians fight for Mandalore, not the Republic.
relationship_notes.bounty_hunters_guild: Many individual Mandalorians work as bounty hunters, and Mandalorian combat skills are highly prized by the Guild. The relationship is professional, not political — clan obligations always supersede guild contracts.
relationship_notes.hutt_cartel: Mandalorian mercenaries have worked for the Hutts throughout history. The Hutts pay well and do not ask questions about Mandalorian politics, making them a convenient source of income for exiled clans.
relationship_notes.black_sun: Minimal direct interaction. Black Sun's covert methods are culturally alien to Mandalorian directness, though individual Mandalorian mercenaries may take Black Sun contracts.

prominent_figures.name: Duchess Satine Kryze
prominent_figures.notes: Championed pacifism and diplomatic integration with the Republic. Her assassination by Maul effectively ended the New Mandalorian movement as a political force, though its ideals persist among some civilians.
prominent_figures.network_assessment: Satine is dead — killed by Maul — but the pacifist movement she built didn't die with her. Her ideals persist in Mandalorian civilian populations who remember what peace looked like. Her ghost shapes every political debate on Mandalore.
prominent_figures.wants: Was driven by the belief that Mandalore's future lay in diplomacy and integration, not warfare. Her legacy is the proof that another path existed.
prominent_figures.secret: Her relationship with Obi-Wan Kenobi gave her an indirect connection to the Jedi Order that she never publicly acknowledged — a pacifist Mandalorian with Jedi ties was a political impossibility.

behavior.under_pressure: Stood firm on principle even when surrounded by enemies. Her courage was diplomatic rather than martial, which made it harder for her opponents to counter.
behavior.when_losing: Appealed to institutions and alliances rather than force. She believed in the system until the system failed her.
behavior.loyalty: Loyal to Mandalore's people, not to any warrior tradition. She saw the warrior culture as the disease, not the cure.
behavior.tells: Historical pattern: when Satine made public statements about peace, she was privately negotiating with Republic allies for support against Death Watch.

useful_to_players: Her legacy creates a civilian population on Mandalore that is sympathetic to non-violent approaches and resistant to both Death Watch and Imperial authority
New Mandalorian sympathizers exist in positions of civilian governance that the warrior factions overlook
Invoking her name carries weight with certain Mandalorian factions and generates hostility from others — use accordingly
hooks: Someone's been distributing copies of Satine's speeches in the bio-dome cities. The Empire banned them, which predictably made them more popular.
A New Mandalorian civilian leader was arrested by Saxon's forces last week for 'seditious assembly.' The charge was discussing agricultural policy. That's how tight the occupation has become.

prominent_figures.name: Pre Vizsla
prominent_figures.notes: Governor of Concordia and secret commander of Death Watch. Wielded the Darksaber and allied with the Separatists and later the Shadow Collective to overthrow the New Mandalorian government. Killed by Maul in single combat.
prominent_figures.network_assessment: Pre Vizsla is dead — killed by Maul for the Darksaber — but Death Watch survived him. He built the militant infrastructure that still operates under different leadership. His legacy is the belief that Mandalore can only be reclaimed through force.
prominent_figures.wants: Was driven by the restoration of Mandalorian warrior culture through the overthrow of the New Mandalorian government. Achieved it, then lost everything to Maul.
prominent_figures.secret: His alliance with the Separatists and later the Shadow Collective demonstrated a willingness to use any external power to achieve Mandalorian goals — a precedent that later Death Watch leaders followed with the Empire.

behavior.under_pressure: Escalated. Vizsla responded to every setback by seeking more powerful allies and more extreme methods.
behavior.when_losing: Doubled down. His challenge of Maul to single combat when the odds had already turned against him was characteristic — pride overrode survival instinct.
behavior.loyalty: Loyal to the warrior ideal of Mandalore, which he defined in his own image. Personal honor and clan pride were inseparable from his political goals.
behavior.tells: Historical pattern: when Vizsla began making public statements about governance, he was privately coordinating military operations. The politics were always cover for the assault.

useful_to_players: Death Watch remnants still follow his playbook — alliance with external powers, covert military buildup, then sudden strike
His failure demonstrates the risk of bringing outside forces into Mandalorian affairs — the Shadow Collective consumed the revolution from within
His Darksaber claim established the precedent that the weapon legitimizes authority — whoever holds it now carries his legacy
hooks: Death Watch cells on Concordia are still using supply caches that Vizsla established before his death. The infrastructure outlasted the leader.
Someone recovered a recording of Vizsla's last speech to Death Watch before the Maul challenge. It's circulating among militant factions as a rallying artifact.

prominent_figures.name: Fenn Rau
prominent_figures.notes: Commander of the Mandalorian Protectors on Concord Dawn. Attempted to maintain Mandalorian autonomy through pragmatic cooperation with the Empire. Eventually allied with the Rebellion after Imperial betrayal.
prominent_figures.network_assessment: Fenn Rau tried the pragmatic path — cooperate with the Empire, preserve what you can. The Empire betrayed him anyway. Now he's with the Rebellion, which tells you everything about how the occupation is going for Mandalorians who play by Imperial rules.
prominent_figures.wants: Mandalorian survival and autonomy by whatever means remain viable. He shifted from Imperial cooperation to Rebel alliance when the calculus changed.
prominent_figures.secret: His Protector training and Clone Wars combat experience make him one of the most tactically capable Mandalorian leaders still active — a military asset the Rebellion is only beginning to understand.

behavior.under_pressure: Calm and disciplined. His Protector training produces measured responses where other Mandalorian leaders might charge in.
behavior.when_losing: Adapts strategy rather than escalating force. His pragmatism allows him to accept temporary defeat in service of long-term objectives.
behavior.loyalty: Loyal to Mandalore first, to the Protectors second, and to whatever alliance currently serves Mandalorian interests. The Rebellion is a means, not a cause.
behavior.tells: When Rau begins training non-Mandalorian fighters in Mandalorian tactics, he's investing in the alliance — which means he's committed for the foreseeable future.

useful_to_players: His Protector connections provide access to Mandalorian military expertise and potentially Fang fighter support
His pragmatic worldview makes him approachable for non-ideological operators who need Mandalorian cooperation
His Rebel alliance means he can serve as a bridge between independent operators and Alliance resources
hooks: Rau's been reaching out to Protector veterans who scattered after the Imperial betrayal. He's rebuilding a unit, which means he's planning an operation that needs Mandalorian-grade warriors.
A Rebel cell in the Mandalore sector received Fang fighter tactical data from an anonymous source. The formatting matches Protector training manuals.

prominent_figures.name: Gar Saxon
prominent_figures.notes: Former Death Watch member appointed by the Empire to govern Mandalore. His willingness to use Imperial authority against his own people makes him despised by traditionalists across all factions.
prominent_figures.network_assessment: Gar Saxon sold out Mandalore to the Empire for a title. Every clan despises him, but he has Imperial Star Destroyers backing his authority. He's a collaborator with a garrison, and that combination is hard to dislodge without a plan.
prominent_figures.wants: Maintenance of his Viceroy position and the Imperial backing that sustains it. Without the Empire, he has no power base — every clan would turn on him immediately.
prominent_figures.secret: His Death Watch background means he knows the militant networks from the inside — he uses that knowledge to suppress exactly the kind of uprising he once led.

behavior.under_pressure: Calls in Imperial reinforcements. Saxon's first response to any challenge is to escalate through Imperial channels rather than handle it through Mandalorian authority.
behavior.when_losing: Becomes more repressive. Confiscates beskar, restricts clan movement, and arrests vocal opponents — measures that increase resistance faster than they suppress it.
behavior.loyalty: Loyal to the Empire because it gives him power. If the Empire abandoned Mandalore, Saxon would have no allies and no survival prospects.
behavior.tells: When Saxon increases beskar confiscation raids, he's either been pressured by Imperial superiors for materials or is preparing to suppress a specific clan he's identified as a threat.

useful_to_players: His dependence on Imperial backing means cutting his communication with Imperial command isolates him entirely
His universal unpopularity among Mandalorian clans means almost any Mandalorian contact will provide intelligence against him willingly
His repressive measures push previously neutral clans toward active resistance — every crackdown creates new allies for his opponents
hooks: Saxon just confiscated beskar from three clans that were previously considered cooperative. He's either desperate for materials or eliminating potential threats preemptively.
An Imperial supply ship scheduled for Saxon's garrison was delayed by 'mechanical failure' at a Mandalorian-crewed drydock. Passive resistance is becoming organized.

prominent_figures.name: Sabine Wren
prominent_figures.notes: A Mandalorian weapons expert who joined the Rebellion. Her possession and eventual relinquishment of the Darksaber became central to Mandalorian reunification efforts.
prominent_figures.network_assessment: Sabine Wren is a Mandalorian who chose the Rebellion, which makes her a bridge between two worlds that don't naturally overlap. Her Darksaber involvement put her at the center of Mandalorian reunification politics whether she wanted it or not.
prominent_figures.wants: Freedom for Mandalore from Imperial occupation. She fights through the Rebellion because it's the most effective path to that goal.
prominent_figures.secret: She created a weapon during her Imperial Academy days that was designed to target beskar armor specifically — a weapon that could be used against Mandalorians. The guilt from that drives much of her current commitment.

behavior.under_pressure: Creative and improvisational. Her weapons expertise and artistic temperament produce unconventional solutions to tactical problems.
behavior.when_losing: Falls back on Mandalorian warrior training — disciplined withdrawal, protecting allies, maintaining unit cohesion.
behavior.loyalty: Loyal to Clan Wren, to her Rebel crew, and to Mandalore. These loyalties occasionally conflict, and when they do, Mandalore wins.
behavior.tells: When Sabine starts painting — on walls, on armor, on equipment — she's processing. The art comes before the action, and the action is usually decisive.

useful_to_players: Her dual role as Rebel operative and Mandalorian clan member gives her access to both networks simultaneously
Her weapons expertise makes her an invaluable technical resource for operations requiring demolitions, sabotage, or creative problem-solving
Her Mandalorian connections can open doors with clans that would otherwise refuse to deal with outsiders
hooks: Sabine sent an encrypted message to Clan Wren through non-Rebel channels last week. When she communicates outside Alliance systems, it's Mandalorian business.
A piece of graffiti matching Sabine's artistic style appeared on an Imperial garrison wall on Krownest. It said 'Remember Mandalore.' The garrison commander tripled his patrols.

source_material_notes: Collapse of the Republic provides the most detailed treatment of Mandalorian political factions during the Clone Wars — Death Watch, New Mandalorians, and the Shadow Collective period. Dawn of Rebellion covers the Imperial occupation, Gar Saxon's Viceroyship, and the Protectors' situation. Friends Like These details Mandalorian clan culture and honor systems. Keeping the Peace includes Mandalorian warrior traditions and equipment.
